13.grammar: A definite noun on the intensive 'faʿʿāl' pattern, which conveys 'one who does an act constantly or to a great degree' — here, one who creates without limit. The al- makes it 'the'. The final -u is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the subject of a sentence or a predicate following the verb 'to be'.
13.root: خ-ل-ق (kh-l-q) — to create, originate, fashion, bring into existence

14.meaning: The All-Knowing — one whose knowledge is complete, perfect, and all-encompassing; an intensive form stressing that knowing is an essential, constant attribute.
14.grammar: A definite noun/adjective in an intensive pattern (faʿīl) that stresses depth and permanence of the quality. The prefix 'al-' means 'the'; the final -u (ḍamma) marks the nominative case, which typically signals the subject of a sentence or a predicate describing it.

1.meaning: 'Only / nothing but' — a restrictive particle that limits and emphasizes, asserting that the matter is exclusively so and no other ('it is only...'). It combines the emphatic 'inna' with the restricting 'mā'.
1.grammar: A compound particle formed from the emphatic inna ('indeed') and mā, which together work as a tool of restriction meaning 'only / nothing but'. It both stresses and confines the statement that follows to a single truth, excluding all alternatives.

2.meaning: His matter, affair, command, or concern — the noun 'amr' covers a directive/command as well as a state of affairs or business; with the attached pronoun it means 'his affair' or 'his command'.
2.grammar: A masculine noun carrying the -u (nominative) ending, which generally marks the word as a subject or the thing being described/named. The attached -hu means 'his' or 'its', showing possession.
2.root: ء-م-ر (ʾ-m-r) — to command, to order; matter/affair

3.meaning: 'When' — a particle introducing a time or circumstance, generally pointing to something expected or definite to come ('when/whenever it happens'). It sets up a condition or moment whose outcome then follows.
3.grammar: An indeclinable adverb/particle of time; it has no case ending and never changes form. It typically introduces a clause about a future or recurring event ('when …'), and is normally followed by a verb describing what takes place.

4.meaning: A verb meaning 'he intended', 'he willed', or 'he meant' — to direct one's purpose toward something, to want or aim at it.
4.grammar: Past-tense (perfect) verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'), in the derived (form IV) pattern arāda. The bare stem with a final -a denotes a completed action by a single male subject, with the sense of actively willing or purposing something.
4.root: ر-و-د (r-w-d) — to seek, want, aim at

5.meaning: Means 'a thing / something / anything' — the most general word for an entity, matter, or item, whether concrete or abstract.
5.grammar: An indefinite noun. The ending -an is the indefinite accusative (tanwīn / 'nunation'): the accusative case marks it as the object of a verb or in an adverbial role, and the final -n marks it as indefinite ('a thing / something'). It is frequently used to mean 'anything' or 'at all'.
5.root: ش-ي-أ (sh-y-') — thing; willing, wishing

6.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
6.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

7.meaning: A verb meaning '(that) He says / utters / speaks'. The core sense is to express something in words.
7.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb, Form I, of a hollow root (the middle root letter is a weak 'w'). The prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'); it carries a shadda (doubling mark) because the preceding word's final consonant assimilates into the yā', a written sandhi feature rather than part of the verb itself. The final -a is the subjunctive ending, used after particles such as 'that', giving 'that He say'. So: 'that He should say / speak'.
7.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak, utter

8.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
8.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

9.meaning: The command 'Be!' — an order to come into existence, the creative imperative by which a thing is summoned into being.
9.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to one person: 'Be!' It is the shortened command form of the verb 'to be/become,' with the bare, vowel-less ending typical of a singular order.
9.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to come into existence

10.meaning: 'And it comes to be / and it is' — the act of existence following upon a command, expressing that something duly comes into being.
10.grammar: The connector 'fa-' ('so/and then') joined to a present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('it is/becomes'). The final -u is the indicative ending, marking an ordinary, unconditioned present or future statement; the doer 'it/he' is built into the verb.
10.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to come into existence

1.meaning: An exclamation declaring Allah utterly free of every flaw and beyond all that is unworthy: 'So glory be (to)…!' / 'How far removed in perfection (is)…!'. The core word affirms transcendence — that the One praised is exalted above any defect, partner, or limitation.
1.grammar: The prefix fa- is a connective ('so/then/therefore'). subḥān is a verbal noun used to proclaim absolute purity and freedom from imperfection. The final -a is the accusative ending: this word stands in a fixed accusative as an exclamatory verbal noun ('glory be!'), and is regularly followed by a noun in the possessive ('… be to/of …').
1.root: س-ب-ح (s-b-ḥ) — to glorify, declare free of imperfection; to swim/move swiftly

2.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
2.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

3.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in his hand,' i.e. in his possession, power, or control — the hand standing figuratively for authority over a matter.
3.grammar: The prefix bi- is a preposition ('in', 'with', 'by'). Because of it, the noun 'hand' takes the -i genitive ending. The attached -hi is a third-person masculine singular possessive pronoun ('his'); the vowel is 'hi' (rather than 'hu') because it follows the -i sound.
3.root: ي-د-ي (y-d-y) — hand; by extension power, possession, agency

4.meaning: Means 'dominion / sovereign kingdom / the realm of total control'. An intensive form of 'kingdom' (mulk), it conveys an all-embracing, absolute sovereignty over all that exists.
4.grammar: A noun on an intensive '-ūt' pattern that magnifies the idea of 'kingship/dominion' (mulk) into total, all-encompassing sovereignty. The final -u is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the subject of a sentence or a predicate after the verb 'to be'. It is typically followed by a possessive ('the dominion of …').

5.meaning: 'every,' 'each,' or 'all' — a word expressing totality or completeness. It indicates the entirety of something: when joined to a singular indefinite noun it means 'every (single) one,' and when joined to a definite noun it can mean 'all of' or 'the whole of.'
5.grammar: A noun of totality. The final '-i' ending is genitive (the 'of/possession' case): it marks the word as governed by a preceding preposition or as the first term of a possessive link to a following noun, so it typically reads 'of every…' or 'every…' leading into what follows.
5.root: ك-ل-ل (k-l-l) — totality, comprising the whole

6.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
6.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
6.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

7.meaning: 'And to Him / and towards Him' — combining 'and,' the directional preposition 'to/towards,' and a pronoun referring to a single male (here, ultimately Allah).
7.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') plus the preposition 'ilā' ('to/towards'), which takes the special form 'ilay-' when a pronoun attaches. The suffix -hi means 'him/it' (third-person masculine singular); its -i vowel is the standard form after a preceding 'y' sound.
7.root: — (preposition and pronoun; no triliteral root)

8.meaning: A verb meaning 'you (all) are brought back / returned' — to be made to go back to a point of origin. The passive voice frames the subjects as acted upon, not acting.
8.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) passive verb, Form I. In the passive the vowel pattern (tu-…-a-) shows the subject is being acted upon: 'you are returned' rather than 'you return'. The tu- prefix marks a second-person subject ('you'), and the -ūna ending marks masculine plural ('you all') and indicative mood (a real, ongoing or certain event). Together: 'you all are brought back / returned'.
8.root: ر-ج-ع (r-j-ʿ) — to return, go back, bring back
